subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Obtain Capabilities - Exploits with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Attack simulation, step 1 of 8. Choosing the target appliance. The attacker picks an internet-facing target, such as a VPN gateway or web application, lists the software versions in use, and needs working exploit code for those versions.

steps.title: Delivering the exploit
steps.caption: The actor fires the exploit against the chosen target. The attempt shows up as an abnormal URI path with a scanner user agent.
steps.defender: The exploit attempt appears in web and WAF logs, and IDS rules for the exploit fire. This is the strongest network signal in the chain.

steps.title: Post-exploit tooling drop
steps.caption: Exploitation succeeded on a monitored host. The exploited server process writes attacker tools into a temp folder or webroot and runs them to hold the access.
steps.defender: Sysmon and EDR show the server process writing executables into temp or webroot. Exploitation is now confirmed on the host.

steps.title: SOC correlates and responds
steps.caption: The SOC joins the IDS alert, the KEV entry, and the patch status of the device, then calls an emergency patch and isolates the affected host.
steps.defender: Correlation of KEV status, patch state, and signatures turns small signals into a confirmed case. Patching and isolation close the gap.
